answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: let the challenge probing adapt: it keeps issuing tasks the fleet already failed, because sparrow only stays cheap while repeat infrastructure gets no useful signal and its pass rate degrades each epoch. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any oasis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
